content.comment_body: Hello all, I have a project where I need to connect to three [product_name] PLCs and collect historical data for analog measurements. I plan to use the [product_name] Access Tool, but my question is: Is it possible to connect to three separate [product_name] devices with this tool, and if so, how? Should I create three Excel files with configurations for the three IPs?

No. The [product_name] Access Tool is only able to communicate with a single [product_name] device. To gather data from the other two devices, you will need to transfer their data over the network to the one that interfaces with the Access Tool.
Thank you. This raises another question: Does [company_name] [product_name] support STRING data types?
No. The [product_name] supports only the following data types: Bool, Integer, and Double Integer.

To help more effectively, please specify in detail what you want to achieve. First, you mention recording analog values from three [product_name] controllers, then ask about string data types. As [user_name] mentioned, it's possible to collect data on one [product_name] controller and record analog values using the Access Tool. You could also use [product_name] software itself to generate a CSV file. It might also be feasible to run three instances of [product_name] software with three controllers, although I haven't tested this yet. If your requirements differ, describe them clearly.

Hello, I need to log data from three [product_name] devices and save this data in three different .csv files on a computer (e.g., Device1.csv, Device2.csv, Device3.csv—these are just sample file names).

Try the method I described: open the [product_name] software three times, select Tools -> Transfer -> I/O Status for each controller, and set the log file names as desired. You can find further details in the online help section of [product_name] software.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are exploring ways to use the [product_name] Access Tool to collect historical analog measurement data from multiple PLC modules. The tool is limited to connecting one device at a time, making multi-device data acquisition more challenging. Users are also asking about support for additional data types and approaches for exporting data to separate CSV files, highlighting restricted multi-device capabilities and limited data type support.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] Access Tool to connect to several PLC devices simultaneously and save data to separate CSV files with ease. They also wish for broader data type support, especially STRING, to improve flexibility in managing collected data.
